pr.title: Give `trip enter` a fresh shell after you log out, not the dead session
pr.head: 5211d92490b725b17a89fcbd9c636f184db73635

summary: trip runs a daemon that keeps terminal sessions alive while clients attach to and detach from them. When a session's command exits, such as a shell you leave with Ctrl-D, the daemon keeps the session as an exited session (the code calls it a corpse) until the next SIGCHLD sweep removes it, so that trip attach can still show what the command left on screen.

That gap broke trip enter <name>. It attaches first and creates the session only when the attach reports the name missing, so right after a logout it attached to the exited session: you saw the old screen, keystrokes went nowhere, and the client never returned. A remote mosh host -- trip enter <name> hung instead of giving you a new shell.

This change gives the Attach request a live flag. enter sets it, and the daemon then removes an exited session that no client holds before it looks the name up, so enter falls through to creating a fresh session. Every other attach passes live: false and still shows an exited session. trip send to an exited session now fails instead of reporting success.
The review found one gap: from inside another session, trip enter <name> uses a different request, SwitchSession, which still moves you onto the exited session.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Exited session (corpse): a session whose command has ended but which the daemon still holds in its map, showing the command's final screen.
  • Unheld: no client is attached to the session, so client_count() == 0.
  • SIGCHLD sweep: the daemon's reap_children loop, which marks a session exited and removes exited sessions no client holds. It runs only when some child of the daemon exits.
  • live: the new Attach field. When true, an unheld exited session counts as missing.

cards.title: Compatibility
cards.html:
• live is #[serde(default)], so an older client's request reads as live: false.
  • Request does not deny unknown fields, so an older daemon ignores live and keeps today's behavior.
  • The running daemon needs a restart on the new binary for the fix to apply.

groups.title: The live flag on the wire
groups.kicker: A new field on the Attach request says the caller needs a running session.
intro: The client and daemon talk in JSON control frames whose shapes live in src/daemon/protocol.rs. The Attach request gains live, a boolean that defaults to false, so the wire format stays readable by both older and newer binaries.

groups.title: The daemon clears an unheld exited session
groups.kicker: Attach with live removes the corpse first; send refuses an exited session.
intro: The daemon now has one helper, remove_unheld_corpse, that drops a named session when its command has exited and no client holds it. CreateSession already did this inline, and now calls the helper. The Attach handler calls it when live is set, before the loop that looks the name up, so the lookup reports session '<name>' not found and the client creates the session.
SendInput now answers an exited session with session '<name>' has exited (<code>), because nothing reads that session's input any more.

checks.text: A session held by a client, such as one a trip attach viewer is watching, is never cleared. Only a session that nobody is looking at is replaced.

files.note: Extracts remove_unheld_corpse, calls it from Attach when live is set, and makes SendInput refuse an exited session.

checks.text: SendInput has one sender, trip send, so the new error reaches no other caller. Checked by searching every use of Request::SendInput.

groups.title: Callers choose live or not
groups.kicker: Only enter's first attach asks for a live session.
intro: attach::attach takes a new live argument, and every caller passes it explicitly. enter passes true on its first attach, then false on the attach after it creates the session, so a command that exits at once is still shown rather than cleared and reported missing. trip attach, trip new, and trip wrap pass false, so deliberate viewing of an exited session is unchanged.

files.note: enter asks for a live session on its first attach and shows whatever it created on the second.

checks.text: When TRIP_SESSION is set, enter returns earlier through SwitchSession, so this live attach runs only from a terminal that is not already in a session.

files.note: attach takes live and puts it on the request.
trip wrap builds its own Attach request and passes live: false.

groups.title: Documentation and the end-to-end check
groups.kicker: The README describes the new behavior, and a new script reproduces the logout case.
intro: The README now says that trip enter <name> treats an exited session as missing, that trip attach shows an exited session's last screen, and that trip send fails on one. tests/exited_session_e2e.py runs its own daemon in a temporary HOME, logs out of a /bin/sh session, enters it again with no trip ls in between, and checks that the new shell is live.

checks.text: At this head, cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo test (132 passed), tests/switcher_e2e.py, and tests/screen_panic_e2e.py pass, and tests/exited_session_e2e.py passed three runs in a row.

files.note: Documents the new behavior of enter, attach, and send on an exited session.

checks.text: Open finding: inside a session, trip enter <name> sends SwitchSession, whose handler spawns only when the name is absent, so it still moves you onto an unheld exited session, contrary to this line. The suggested fix is to call remove_unheld_corpse(&mut sessions, &to) before the contains_key check in that handler.

files.note: New end-to-end check for entering a session again after logging out of it.
